title: Untangle client surface and bump runtime deps across Python/JS/Go SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need to perform a coordinated dependency upgrade and API surface cleanup across the Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket covers: 1) bumping runtime and build dependencies (requests/urllib3, node-fetch/undici, go-http libs, protobuf, opt-in TLS/KMS clients); 2) removing deprecated API surface (old streaming endpoints + legacy field aliases) with non-breaking fallbacks for one release; and 3) small refactors to simplify client initialization so downstream code avoids fragile shims.

Why now:
- Multiple security and performance fixes are available in upstream libs (TLS updates, HTTP/2 client patches, JSON parsing improvements).
- We are carrying per-language shims for legacy API shapes that increase maintenance cost and cause occasional regressions in typed SDKs.
- Upcoming runtime-1.18 and sdk-2026.03 releases expect consistent client behavior.

Scope & goals:
- Upgrade pinned dependencies to latest compatible stable releases across Python/JS/Go and regenerate lockfiles.
- Remove legacy API helpers (client.legacy_stream, responses.old_tokens) and keep transparent compatibility wrappers for one release that log DeprecationWarnings but delegate to new endpoints.
- Replace ad-hoc backoff/retry helpers with shared retry util in each SDK where feasible.
- Run full CI matrix, add new unit tests covering deprecated surface delegation and upgraded library behavior.
- Provide migration guide and automated codemods for common breaking patterns.

Non-goals:
- Major API redesigns (this ticket should not change request/response semantics beyond removing aliases).
- Large refactors of high-level features (e.g., reimplementing streaming infra).

Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs compile and pass CI (unit + integration against staging endpoint).
- No open security alerts from dependency scanners for updated packages.
- Deprecation warnings emitted for removed fields for at least one release path and documented migration steps in the SDK CHANGELOG and CONSOLE docs.
- Release notes drafted and validated by PM and DevEx before merge.

Rollout plan:
1) Create per-language feature branches (ENG-19735: python, ENG-19736: js, ENG-19737: go).
2) Upgrade deps, run tests, fix failing tests, and create PRs with a standardized PR template listing changed direct deps and notable transitive updates.
3) Deploy canary packages to internal pip/npm/goproxy with tag @internal/canary.
4) Validate internal services and samples (redwood-demo, inference-bench) against canary packages for 72 hours.
5) Promote to stable and publish migration guide.

Rollback strategy:
- If a runtime break is detected, revert the SDK release and publish a compatibility patch on the previous release channel. For dependency-caused runtime issues, pin to previous known-good transitive versions and open a follow-up to debug upstream changes.

Notes and references:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/SDK+Dep+Upgrade+Plan
- Initial dependency scan (Mar 2026): https://depscan.redwood/team-reports/sdk-march-2026
- Example failing case observed in staging: JSON streaming chunk boundary behavior changed for node-fetch v3.x; tracked in ENG-19736 PR comments.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Patel: Kicked off spike to enumerate direct and transitive deps across SDKs. Found 12 transitive CVEs flagged; prioritizing upgrades to urllib3, node-fetch/undici, and go-net/http backports.
2026-03-04 - Marco Ruiz: Created python branch ENG-19735 and started bumping requests from 2.31.0 -> 2.33.0. Found a change in retry semantics; added unit tests to assert backoff behavior.
2026-03-05 - DevEx reviewer (Lina Chen): Reviewed python PR, requested explicit DeprecationWarning for deprecated 'old_tokens' field and an opt-out env var REDWOOD_WARN_DEPRECATIONS=false.

2026-03-07 - Marco Ruiz: Opened JS branch ENG-19736. Node CI failing due to node-fetch streaming behavior (PR #4201). Temporarily switched to undici in canary to validate behavior; requires small adapter in streamToAsyncIterator().
2026-03-09 - Security (Tomás Ortega): Confirmed no high severity issues remain after targeted upgrades. Minor crypto config change required for Go TLS handshake; added note in release candidates.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Integration run against staging with canary packages completed for Python and Go. JS canary still has intermittent chunking test failures; tracking under JS PR comments. Plan: land python/go first and keep JS as canary until fix upstream or implement a localized patch.

2026-03-12 - PM review (Evelyn Park): Approved migration docs draft and scheduled sdk-2026.03 release notes review on 2026-03-15. Confirmed migration guidance adequate for enterprise customers using Dedicated and Private deployments.
